open_items.text: Mailchimp shows a banner that a plan downgrade couldn't finish because of account conflicts. Check that it doesn't affect sending or audience limits.

checkin.bottom_line: Nothing shows the program is failing, and nothing yet shows it works. The copy mostly holds up and no email needs a rewrite. The risks are a few links and details to fix before the next sends, targeting that uses grade band and first name only, and measurement: with no holdout group, the page can't show that emails move teachers between phases.
working: Scope is clear. "In the program" means claimed and oriented teachers in Medium, Large and Enterprise districts. Rostered teachers are pre-marketing and owned by the partner experience team.
The copy follows the program's rules: one button per email, K–2 and 3–5 versions where it matters, and a plain voice that leads with the teacher's judgment.
Flows start from Gainsight phase changes, so each teacher gets emails that match where they are.

fixes.issue: The digital-background link isn't confirmed, and its gallery tracking ID differs from the others.
fixes.fix: Open the link, confirm the destination, and align the tracking ID.

fixes.issue: The quote is auto-transcribed and has no attribution. T4 was the biggest send (12,141 on Oct 2).
fixes.fix: Check the transcription and add attribution before new teachers enter Discovery.

fixes.issue: The tracking ID is a placeholder.
fixes.fix: Replace it with the real ID.

fixes.issue: The open flag looks stale. The copy changelog shows the lesson names were verified on 8/20.

annoy: T3 can tell a teacher on a normal schedule that they're behind. Confirm the pacing field is wired up, or pause T3 for districts on alternating schedules.
T4 to T7 are written as "a few days after" the last email. If the real waits are short, a teacher could get four emails in about a week. Check the waits in Mailchimp.
T16 links a course whose outcome reads as coach-facing, which may not fit a classroom teacher.
gaps: Personalization is first name and grade band only. No email knows where a teacher is in their unit.
Gainsight flags count activity since 7/1/2026, so a returning teacher can look new and enter an early flow.
There is no comparison group, so the page shows movement between phases but can't show whether the emails caused it. Phase movement is read as direction, not proof.
checkin.scale_title: Scaling to Inkwell and Great First Eight
scale: The structure carries over: phase segments, Gainsight-triggered flows, this registry and the weekly snapshot.
Each program needs its own copy and its own registry file. The Inquiry Journeys copy doesn't transfer.
Reporting can then roll up by program on this page, with the same scorecard for each.
next: Extend the Tuesday snapshot routine to check each email's expected versus actual sends, flat flows, unsubscribes over 1% and bounces. It adds no new scheduled function.
caveats: Mailchimp opens and clicks are inflated by link scanners and Apple Mail's privacy feature. Judge the program by Gainsight phase movement, not by clicks.
The Mailchimp connection reads analytics only. It can't show whether each of the six flows is live or paused, so that needs a manual check in Mailchimp.

The flows were paused in October for edits and restarted, and Mailchimp lists them as Active since Oct 20. The exact pause dates aren't recorded, so the Started counts in Mailchimp cover only the time since the restart.
